claim: The 1600-token limit refuses every RED/GREEN step of STP-20: its Frame without Prior art and Size is about 810 tokens alone, step 1 about 3000 tokens, step 2 about 2400, step 4 over 2000; STP-21's own step 1 lands at about 1550.
A range broken over a line (STP-20 step 1: `AC-3 to` at a line end, `AC-9)` after indentation on the next) is not said to match, so a per-line match drops AC-4 to AC-8.
Whole-word term matching misses inflected uses: `named criteria` (Named criterion), `a step test` (Step tests), STP-20 `is done` (Done step), so briefs lack the definitions their criteria need.
A term line with two bold names (STP-20 `- **Fact line**: ... **Action line**: ...`) yields only the first term.

next names stapel brief even when that brief refuses (too large, unknown id), so the orchestrator loops on a failing command; the JSON path becoming null for build-step and green-step is not stated in Guarantees.
An exclusion in the step (STP-20 step 1: `AC-1 without next::writes_nothing`) is ignored, so the tests line tells the builder to make the excluded test pass.
The brief lacks the rows of the Test plan's main table, which hold the test cases a builder writes (STP-20 step 1c's Coverage rows are the whole content of the step).
A step whose id-like words find neither a criterion nor a finding (no findings.jsonl) gives a brief of Frame and step only with exit 0.
AC-9 `digits with at most one lowercase letter` admits `c2`; say digits followed by at most one lowercase letter.
Range forms with an en dash or dots (`AC-3–AC-5`, `AC-3..AC-5`) silently select only the ends.
The term rule reads any Spec line `- **<name>**: ...`; the Guarantees lines could be read as terms; the term list should be bounded to the Terms list.
AC-7 does not say a row names a step test by an equal backticked name, so a substring match could select `next::first_open_step_x`.
A Plan with the step label twice: the brief does not say whether it takes the first, the last or refuses.
For n > m AC-11 says the Spec does not have the range, which is false when both rows exist; a separate text would not mislead.
Bytes / 4 underestimates this text (about 3 to 3.5 bytes per token), so 1600 estimated tokens is about 2000 real ones.

AC-17 changes the action of most existing next tests: their fixture Plan `1. One.` names no criterion, so build-step becomes a brief refusal and write-section Plan, against step 8's Must not change and the Guarantees.
The term Names a test never enters a brief: AC-7 and AC-8 say `names a step test`, which does not use the term's words.

brief::writes_nothing, brief::closed_ticket and brief::empty_parts_are_left_out pass before the code as written (they assert only equality or absence), so they are coverage tests the Plan does not list.
Step 1 must print the tests header line of AC-2, which needs criterion rows and ranges specified only in step 3.
AC-4 prints the step item as written, while the term Step item collapses whitespace; the golden file can satisfy only one.
STP-21 step 1 is about 1505 of 1600 estimated tokens; the orchestrator rule cannot run for this ticket before the command exists.
AC-17 fixes the subject `Plan` while next uses the configured title of the plan section; the Guarantees do not name the new fact kind of next.
For `stapel brief abc-1 2` the spec does not say whether KEY in the title and the path is the folder key or the given key.
A findings.jsonl that cannot be read as a whole (a directory, not UTF-8) is in neither AC-10 nor the Inputs row.
No fixture Plan has a blank line after a step item, so the end-at-blank-line rule of the Step item is never exercised; removing it passes every test.
Only `base: none` is tested; a constant `none` would pass every test, so the base of state.json is unverified.
Step 1 already implements the refusals of step 2 (legacy, unreadable, no plan section, no step, step twice) without tests, so the step 2 tests of those cases would pass before their code.
The Description is found by the fixed title `Description`, while the Plan title comes from the configuration.
`frame_of` takes a Frame heading of any level, `### Frame ###` is not recognised, and a `#` line in a code fence ends the Frame; no test covers these.
The guard half of `brief::runs_in_an_agent_shell` passes trivially, as the guard allows every non-person stapel subcommand; only the CLAUDECODE half could go RED.
Untested: a lettered step `2c`; a Frame empty after the paragraphs are dropped; a Frame with no heading after it; a KEY given in another case than the folder key.
refuses_a_wrong_call has only rejecting STEP cases; a rule that rejects `2c` would pass it, and empty, non-ASCII and very long STEP values are not pinned.
fate: no change: brief::lettered_step_and_folder_key (step 1c) accepts 2c, so that mutation fails a test; the ASCII-only byte checks are LOW
